title: Discovery of over a thousand variable stars in Terzan 5 and Liller 1 with JWST
comment: 222 pages (51 pages of text plus a 167-page lightcurve atlas), 24 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: The Bulge Fossil Fragments Terzan 5 and Liller 1 host some of the densest stellar environments in the Galaxy, yet their variable star populations have remained largely unexplored due to crowding and heavy obscuration. Here, we identify 1,315 variable sources in these two systems in what is to our knowledge the first JWST time-series variability census of a globular cluster-like object. By differencing consecutive non-destructive reads within each NIRCam integration, we transform sample-up-the-ramp imaging into an infrared movie sampled every 21 seconds. More than a century of observations has cataloged 5,604 variables, the majority of them pulsating stars, across 151 Galactic globular clusters. Our census alone amounts to 23 percent of that total and contains more photometrically variable binaries than had previously been cataloged in all globular clusters combined. The field of Liller 1, with zero previously known variables, now hosts 915, nearly double the count in the runner-up $ω$ Centauri. We detect dramatic infrared variability from the Rapid Burster, revealing the counterpart sought since 1976 (see Desai et al. 2026), and blindly recover a signal coincident with the prototype redback pulsar PSR J1748-2446A at its radio-timed orbital period, identifying the first optical or infrared counterpart to any of Terzan 5's pulsars. More broadly, we present a technique that recovers group-level time-series photometry from JWST observations, enabling time-domain studies with an observatory whose field of view is naturally matched to the Galaxy's densest stellar systems.

AI.tldr: The first JWST time-series variability census of globular-cluster-like systems identifies 1,315 variable sources in Terzan 5 and Liller 1, including the Rapid Burster's long-sought counterpart and the first IR counterpart to a Terzan 5 pulsar.
AI.motivation: Terzan 5 and Liller 1 are among the Galaxy's densest stellar environments, but their variable star populations were essentially unexplored due to severe crowding and obscuration. Existing variability catalogs (5,604 variables across 151 Galactic globular clusters) are thus heavily biased against such highly extincted, crowded bulge systems.
AI.method: Difference consecutive non-destructive reads within each NIRCam integration to convert sample-up-the-ramp imaging into an infrared movie sampled every 21 seconds, yielding group-level time-series photometry from JWST. The resulting light curves are searched for variability across both fields.
AI.result: 1,315 variable sources detected in total. Liller 1, previously with zero known variables, now has 915—nearly double the runner-up ω Centauri. The census contains more photometrically variable binaries than all previously cataloged globular clusters combined, and alone represents 23% of the century-long, 151-cluster total. It reveals dramatic IR variability from the Rapid Burster (its counterpart sought since 1976) and blindly recovers a signal coincident with redback pulsar PSR J1748-2446A at its radio-timed orbital period—the first optical/IR counterpart to any Terzan 5 pulsar.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a technique for recovering group-level time-series photometry from JWST, enabling time-domain studies with an observatory whose field of view is naturally matched to the Galaxy's densest stellar systems.

title: The long period radio transient ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable
summary: Wide-field time-domain radio surveys have recently unveiled a new class of Galactic radio emitter: long period radio transients (LPTs). Despite the rapid pace of discovery, their origins remain poorly understood, with two main theories emerging: slowly spinning magnetars or binary white dwarfs (WDs) with magnetic interactions. All three LPTs with well-characterised optical counterparts are WDs in binary systems, but even within that class there is diversity, with one accreting and two detached systems. In this Letter, we show that the LPT ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable (CV)---a WD accreting from a low-mass companion---with a spectroscopic orbital period consistent with the radio pulse period, and specifically, potentially consistent with being a polar. Unlike the other known LPT CV, ASKAP J1448-68 does not exhibit the He II emission that is a hallmark of magnetic CVs in their high accretion states. We also present new optical time-series and infrared photometric observations, showing flickering at the 10% level and suggesting a possible period bouncer origin. This identification of ASKAP J1448-68 adds to the small sample of characterised LPT counterparts, and shows that LPTs can arise from WD binaries with a range of accretion states.

AI.tldr: The LPT ASKAP J1448-68 is identified as a cataclysmic variable (WD accreting from a low-mass companion), likely a polar, with a spectroscopic orbital period matching its radio pulse period, showing flickering and a possible period bouncer origin.
AI.motivation: Long period radio transients (LPTs) are a newly discovered class of Galactic radio emitters whose origins remain poorly understood, with competing theories of slowly spinning magnetars versus magnetic binary white dwarfs. Characterising optical counterparts is needed to distinguish these scenarios.
AI.method: Optical spectroscopy to measure the orbital period and classify the system, plus new optical time-series and infrared photometric observations to search for variability (flickering) and infer evolutionary status.
AI.result: ASKAP J1448-68 is a cataclysmic variable whose spectroscopic orbital period is consistent with the radio pulse period and potentially consistent with a polar. Unlike the other known LPT CV, it lacks He II emission typical of magnetic CVs in high accretion states. Observations reveal ~10% flickering and suggest a possible period bouncer origin.
AI.conclusion: ASKAP J1448-68 adds to the small sample of characterised LPT counterparts and demonstrates that LPTs can arise from WD binaries spanning a range of accretion states.

title: Beyond what's observed: hierarchical inference of Gaia astrometric compact-object binaries
summary: Astrometry from the Gaia mission has revealed a large and homogeneous population of binaries containing compact objects, including more than 3000 white dwarf--main sequence (WDMS) binaries with orbital periods of $P_{\rm orb}\sim100$--$1000$ d. Most of these binaries likely underwent mass transfer from asymptotic giant branch donors, but their evolutionary histories remain uncertain. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian inference model to constrain the intrinsic properties of the Gaia WDMS binary population while accounting for measurement uncertainties and the survey selection function. We infer the distributions of orbital period, component masses, and eccentricity, as well as the total space density. We find that the intrinsic orbital-period distribution follows a declining power law, $p(P_{\rm orb})\propto P_{\rm orb}^{-0.445\pm0.048}$, and the WD mass distribution is sharply peaked near $0.6\,M_\odot$, with only ~1% of systems hosting WDs more massive than $0.8\,M_\odot$. The inferred MS-star mass distribution is relatively flat down to ~$0.3\,M_{\odot}$, which is unexpected if the population is dominated by products of stable mass transfer with a fixed critical mass ratio. The eccentricity distribution peaks at a nonzero value, $e=0.046\pm0.001$, suggesting incomplete circularization or eccentricity excitation. We infer a midplane space density of ~$3\times10^4\,{\rm kpc}^{-3}$ for WDMS binaries in the parameter space probed by Gaia DR3. These properties provide empirical benchmarks for future work to constrain binary evolution models. We also apply the framework to Gaia black hole and neutron star binaries, inferring that $30^{+66}_{-20}$ and $614^{+203}_{-149}$ such systems exist within 2 kpc, respectively. This framework will enable detailed population-level constraints on a wide range of systems identified from the much larger catalog of astrometric orbits expected from Gaia DR4.

AI.tldr: We develop a hierarchical Bayesian model to infer the intrinsic properties of Gaia WDMS binaries, revealing a declining period distribution, peaked WD masses, a flat MS mass distribution, nonzero eccentricity, and a space density of ~3e4 kpc^-3, with the framework also applied to BH and NS binaries.
AI.motivation: Gaia astrometry has revealed a large homogeneous population of binaries with compact objects, including over 3000 WDMS binaries. Most likely formed through mass transfer from AGB donors, but their evolutionary histories remain uncertain, motivating population-level constraints.
AI.method: A hierarchical Bayesian inference model that constrains intrinsic properties of the Gaia WDMS binary population while accounting for measurement uncertainties and the survey selection function, inferring distributions of orbital period, component masses, eccentricity, and total space density.
AI.result: Intrinsic orbital-period distribution follows a declining power law p(P_orb) ∝ P_orb^-0.445±0.048; WD mass distribution sharply peaked near 0.6 M_sun with ~1% above 0.8 M_sun; MS-star mass distribution relatively flat down to ~0.3 M_sun; eccentricity peaks at e=0.046±0.001; midplane space density ~3e4 kpc^-3 for WDMS binaries in the Gaia DR3 parameter space. For BH and NS binaries, 30+66-20 and 614+203-149 systems exist within 2 kpc, respectively.
AI.conclusion: These properties provide empirical benchmarks for constraining binary evolution models, and the framework will enable detailed population-level constraints on a wide range of systems from the much larger catalog of astrometric orbits expected from Gaia DR4.

title: PHAROS: Panchromatic spectral energy distributions of solar-like stars across evolutionary stages
summary: Panchromatic stellar spectral energy distributions (SEDs) provide the wavelength-dependent irradiation fields required for studies of exoplanet atmospheres, photochemistry, atmospheric escape, and habitability. We present PHAROS, the Panchromatic Habitable-world Archive of Radiation from Observed Solar-like stars, a first release of fifteen component-traceable SEDs for nearby FGK stars spanning adopted ages of 0.26--6.5\,Gyr. The catalogue covers 0.5--5000\,nm and combines archival \textit{XMM-Newton} and \textit{Chandra} high-energy constraints, semiempirical extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) reconstructions, \textit{HST} and \textit{IUE} ultraviolet spectra, Gaia DR3 XP and ancillary optical spectrophotometry, and PHOENIX photospheric extensions. When X-ray data support spectral modelling, target-specific coronal plasma models define the high-energy segment and anchor the EUV normalisation; otherwise, empirical high-energy templates are scaled to literature luminosity constraints. Each SED preserves segment-level provenance, distinguishing directly observed intervals from reconstructed components, empirical templates, bridges, and model-derived extensions. The largest diversity occurs at X-ray, EUV, and ultraviolet wavelengths. Younger age-context groups generally show stronger high-energy output relative to their photospheric continua, although the dispersion within each group shows that age alone does not uniquely determine the irradiation environment. PHAROS provides traceable panchromatic irradiation fields for studies of planetary atmospheres, photochemistry, atmospheric escape, forward modelling, retrievals, and interpretation of future direct-imaging observations, including those anticipated for NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory.

AI.tldr: PHAROS is a first-release archive of fifteen component-traceable panchromatic SEDs (0.5–5000 nm) for nearby FGK stars aged 0.26–6.5 Gyr, combining X-ray, EUV, UV, optical, and model data with segment-level provenance for exoplanet irradiation studies.
AI.motivation: Panchromatic stellar SEDs are needed to characterize wavelength-dependent irradiation that drives exoplanet atmospheric photochemistry, escape, and habitability. Existing data are often fragmented across wavelengths or lack traceability, motivating a unified, provenance-aware catalogue.
AI.method: The authors assemble SEDs from archival XMM-Newton and Chandra high-energy constraints, semiempirical EUV reconstructions, HST and IUE UV spectra, Gaia DR3 XP plus ancillary optical spectrophotometry, and PHOENIX photospheric extensions. Where X-ray data permit spectral modelling, target-specific coronal plasma models define the high-energy segment and anchor EUV normalization; otherwise empirical high-energy templates are scaled to literature luminosities. Each SED retains segment-level provenance.
AI.result: The catalogue covers 0.5–5000 nm for fifteen nearby FGK stars spanning 0.26–6.5 Gyr. Spectral diversity is largest at X-ray, EUV, and UV wavelengths. Younger age groups generally show stronger high-energy output relative to their photospheric continua, but substantial intra-group dispersion indicates age alone does not uniquely determine the irradiation environment.
AI.conclusion: PHAROS delivers traceable panchromatic irradiation fields supporting studies of planetary atmospheres, photochemistry, atmospheric escape, forward modelling, retrievals, and interpretation of future direct-imaging observations, including NASA's Habitable Worlds Observatory.

title: Properties of Circumfacular Regions derived from H$α$ and Ca II K synoptic observations of the Sun
summary: Circumfacular regions are dark chromospheric structures surrounding magnetic regions whose properties and contribution to solar activity diagnostics remain poorly understood. We investigate their photometric and geometric properties using full-disk H$α$ and Ca II K observations acquired by the Chromospheric Telescope (ChroTel) from 2012 to 2020, spanning the maximum and declining phases of solar cycle 24 and the beginning of cycle 25. We develop an automated segmentation algorithm to identify circumfacular regions and define a photometric index analogous to existing excess and deficit indices. We compare their temporal evolution with those of plages, dark features, and filaments on solar-cycle and Carrington-rotation timescales. Circumfacular regions develop after the H$α$ plage brightening become visible and persist into the decay phase of active regions. At activity maximum, they are the most extended chromospheric structures, covering more than half of the visible solar disk. Their mean intensity varies only weakly throughout the solar cycle; consequently, their index variability, as well as that of the other photometric indices, is driven primarily by changes in area coverage. H$α$ and Ca II~K indices are strongly correlated, although their correlations weaken toward solar minimum. This activity-dependent relationship is primarily driven by the decline of the area of H$α$ excess regions during periods of low activity, and the increasing relative contributions of deficit and circumfacular regions. Our results therefore suggest that circumfacular regions should be considered when interpreting disk-integrated chromospheric observations of the Sun and solar-type stars.

AI.tldr: Circumfacular regions are the most extended chromospheric structures at solar maximum, covering over half the visible disk, and their activity-dependent index is driven mainly by area coverage, so they must be considered in disk-integrated chromospheric observations.
AI.motivation: Circumfacular regions are dark chromospheric structures surrounding magnetic regions, yet their properties and contribution to solar activity diagnostics remain poorly understood.
AI.method: Using full-disk H-alpha and Ca II K observations from ChroTel (2012-2020, spanning solar cycle 24 maximum/decline and start of cycle 25), the authors developed an automated segmentation algorithm to identify circumfacular regions and defined a photometric index analogous to existing excess and deficit indices, comparing temporal evolution with plages, dark features, and filaments on solar-cycle and Carrington-rotation timescales.
AI.result: Circumfacular regions develop after H-alpha plage brightening appears and persist into the active-region decay phase. At activity maximum they are the most extended chromospheric structures, covering more than half the visible disk. Their mean intensity varies only weakly over the cycle, so index variability is driven primarily by area coverage changes. H-alpha and Ca II K indices are strongly correlated, with correlations weakening toward solar minimum, driven by the decline of H-alpha excess area at low activity and increasing relative contributions of deficit and circumfacular regions.
AI.conclusion: Circumfacular regions should be considered when interpreting disk-integrated chromospheric observations of the Sun and solar-type stars.

title: LISA Double White Dwarfs in Triple Systems
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: Double white dwarfs (DWDs) in the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) band are major Galactic gravitational-wave sources, but many tight DWD progenitors may reside in hierarchical triples. Triple evolution can alter both the production rate and parameter distributions of LISA DWDs. Using the Multiple Star Evolution (MSE) code, we study how the adiabatic mass-loss model (Ge model) and the SCATTER formalism for triple common-envelope (TCE) evolution affect triple-channel LISA DWD formation. Our main model evolves 10^5 triples with both ingredients. Three control models, each with 10^4 triples, vary the mass-transfer stability criterion to the original MSE polytropic model, remove SCATTER, or adopt low metallicity (Z=0.001). We also evolve 10^6 isolated binaries with the same framework as a binary-channel reference. Systems that are dynamically unstable under the polytropic model can instead undergo stable Roche-lobe overflow under the Ge model. This sustained mass transfer modifies the donor envelope, reduces its binding energy, and helps the subsequent common-envelope phase form a close DWD rather than a merger. The Ge model increases the triple-channel LISA DWD yield by about 60% relative to the polytropic model, while SCATTER changes the integrated yield by only about 3%. After residence-time weighting, triples contribute about 1.3e7 LISA-band DWDs, including 1.4e4 individually resolvable systems. In the combined triple-plus-binary normalization, the binary channel contributes 3.1e6 LISA-band DWDs and 4.7e3 resolvable systems; these are the binary share of the combined population, not the binary-only Galactic estimate. The main triple model has a flatter, higher-q mass-ratio distribution than the polytropic-model triples, is dominated by He-CO and He-He binaries, and produces rare eccentric systems only when a tertiary star remains bound.

AI.tldr: Triple evolution, especially the Ge adiabatic mass-loss model, boosts LISA-band double white dwarf (DWD) production by ~60% versus a polytropic criterion, while SCATTER changes yields by only ~3%; triples dominate resolvable and total LISA DWD numbers under the adopted normalization.
AI.motivation: Tight DWDs in the LISA band are major Galactic gravitational-wave sources, but many progenitors likely reside in hierarchical triples. Triple evolution can change both the formation rate and parameter distributions of LISA DWDs, so the binary-only picture may be incomplete and needs a triple-channel treatment.
AI.method: Using the Multiple Star Evolution (MSE) code, evolve 1e5 triples with the Ge adiabatic mass-loss model plus the SCATTER formalism for triple common-envelope (TCE) evolution. Run three control sets of 1e4 triples: original MSE polytropic mass-transfer stability, no SCATTER, and low metallicity (Z=0.001). Also evolve 1e6 isolated binaries with the same framework as a binary-channel reference.
AI.result: Systems dynamically unstable under the polytropic model can undergo stable Roche-lobe overflow under Ge. Sustained mass transfer modifies the donor envelope, lowers its binding energy, and helps the subsequent common-envelope phase form a close DWD instead of a merger. Ge increases the triple-channel LISA DWD yield by ~60% relative to polytropic; SCATTER changes the integrated yield by only ~3%. After residence-time weighting, triples contribute ~1.3e7 LISA-band DWDs, including ~1.4e4 individually resolvable systems. In the combined triple-plus-binary normalization, the binary channel contributes ~3.1e6 LISA-band DWDs and ~4.7e3 resolvable systems (binary share of the combined population, not a binary-only Galactic estimate). The main triple model has a flatter, higher-q mass-ratio distribution than polytropic triples, is dominated by He-CO and He-He binaries, and produces rare eccentric systems only when a tertiary star remains bound.
AI.conclusion: Mass-transfer stability physics is a leading uncertainty for triple-channel LISA DWD populations: the Ge criterion substantially raises yields and shifts mass-ratio distributions, whereas SCATTER is a minor effect. Triples can be a major contributor to both the total and resolvable LISA DWD population once residence-time weighting and combined normalization are applied.

title: On the frequency-dependent time lags of the intermediate polar V709 Cas
comment: 17 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are binary systems in which a white dwarf (WD) primary accretes material from a late-type secondary, typically via a disc. To date, only six CVs, all of which are non-magnetic, have been found to exhibit lags (delayed variability in one band with respect to another). In all six cases, these lags are ``red'' (i.e., red lags blue) with a time lag of order seconds. While there is no generally accepted mechanism for producing red lags in CVs, current theories suggest reprocessing in the disc, either on the thermal or recombination time-scales, or inside-out shocks propagating through the disc. Using $g$-, $r$-, and $i$-band data from the OPtical TIming CAMera (OPTICAM), we report the discovery of frequency-dependent red lags from V709 Cas: a magnetic CV of the intermediate polar (IP) subclass. These red lags reach a maximum of $\sim$4--6 s on time-scales of 7.4--13.0 min, similar to previously-reported lags in non-magnetic CVs. The detection of lags in an IP is significant as the WD's magnetic field truncates the accretion disc, limiting disc-based lag mechanisms to large radii; as a result, characteristic accretion disc time-scales cannot explain the observed lags. However, recombination can occur on second time-scales, even in systems with truncated discs. For example, we show that recombination in the disc's bright spot, where overflowing material from the secondary meets the outer-edge of the disc, plausibly explains V709 Cas's optical spectrum, the prominence of optical spin-orbit beat pulsations, and the red lags found in this work.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the discovery of frequency-dependent red lags (up to ~4-6 s) in the magnetic intermediate polar V709 Cas using OPTICAM g-, r-, and i-band data, and proposes recombination in the disc's bright spot as the mechanism, since the truncated disc rules out standard disc time-scale explanations.
AI.motivation: Only six cataclysmic variables (all non-magnetic) were previously known to show red lags, and no mechanism is generally accepted; existing theories invoke disc reprocessing (thermal/recombination time-scales) or inside-out shocks. Testing whether lags occur in a magnetic CV whose truncated disc limits disc-based mechanisms would clarify the origin of these lags.
AI.method: High-speed multi-band optical photometry of the intermediate polar V709 Cas using g-, r-, and i-band data from the OPTical TIming CAMera (OPTICAM), with cross-correlation/lag analysis to measure frequency-dependent time delays between bands.
AI.result: Frequency-dependent red lags were detected, reaching a maximum of ~4-6 s on time-scales of 7.4-13.0 min, similar to previously reported lags in non-magnetic CVs. Because the white dwarf's magnetic field truncates the accretion disc, characteristic disc time-scales cannot explain the observed lags; recombination on second time-scales, even in truncated discs, can.
AI.conclusion: The discovery of red lags in the intermediate polar V709 Cas extends lag phenomena to magnetic CVs. The authors show that recombination in the disc's bright spot—where overflowing material from the secondary meets the outer disc edge—plausibly accounts for V709 Cas's optical spectrum, the prominence of optical spin-orbit beat pulsations, and the observed red lags.

title: On the origin of carbon- and oxygen-rich hot subdwarfs: an sdB merger scenario
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 13 pages, 17 figures
summary: Carbon- and oxygen-rich hot subdwarfs (CO-sdO stars) represent an extremely rare subclass of helium-rich hot subdwarfs. Recent observations of PG 1654+322, PG 1528+025, and UCAC4 108 reveal unusually large surface mass fractions of carbon and oxygen, which are difficult to explain within existing formation scenarios. We explore whether mergers involving sdB stars can provide a viable formation channel for these objects. Using the stellar evolution code MESA, we model the post-merger evolution of two merger channels: mergers between two sdB stars and mergers between a helium white dwarf and an sdB star. Carbon and oxygen synthesized during core helium burning in sdB stars may provide a natural chemical reservoir if efficient mixing occurs during the merger. The resulting evolutionary tracks are broadly consistent with the effective temperatures, surface gravities, and luminosities observed for the three stars, suggesting remnant masses of about 0.8-1.0 M_sun. Our calculations suggest that mergers involving sdB stars may represent a viable formation pathway for CO-rich hot subdwarfs.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether mergers involving sdB stars can explain the rare CO-rich hot subdwarfs (CO-sdO), especially PG 1654+322, PG 1528+025, and UCAC4 108, using MESA post-merger evolution models.
AI.motivation: CO-sdO stars are an extremely rare subclass of helium-rich hot subdwarfs. Recent observations of PG 1654+322, PG 1528+025, and UCAC4 108 show unusually large surface carbon and oxygen mass fractions that existing formation scenarios struggle to explain, motivating a search for an alternative formation channel.
AI.method: The authors use the stellar evolution code MESA to model the post-merger evolution of two channels: (1) mergers between two sdB stars and (2) mergers between a helium white dwarf and an sdB star. They consider that carbon and oxygen produced by core helium burning in sdB stars can serve as a chemical reservoir if efficient mixing occurs during the merger.
AI.result: The resulting evolutionary tracks are broadly consistent with the observed effective temperatures, surface gravities, and luminosities of the three stars, implying remnant masses of roughly 0.8-1.0 M_sun.
AI.conclusion: Mergers involving sdB stars may represent a viable formation pathway for carbon- and oxygen-rich hot subdwarfs.

title: Abundance analysis of three new extremely metal-poor stars, including one CEMP-s star
comment: 10 pages - 11 figures - Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary:
We report a detailed abundance analysis of three extremely metal-poor (EMP) stars thanks to spectra obtained with the high-dispersion spectrograph (HDS) at the Subaru telescope.
  The aim is to observe a sample of EMP candidate stars selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and determine their detailed chemical composition. High-resolution spectra of three faint turn-off stars using HDS on the Subaru telescope were acquired.We used standard 1D models to compute the abundances of several elements (Li, C, Mg, Ca, Sr, and Ba). The stars we analysed have a metallicity [Fe/H] of between -3.02 and -3.57 dex. We also measured accurate radial velocities that, coupled with the Gaia astrometric data, allowed us to compute actions and Galactic orbits for the stars.
  Our analysis confirms that the stars are genuine EMP stars. One of them (SDSS J074238.68 +470537.0) can be classified as a CEMP-s star with the highest [Mg/Fe] ratio ever measured in a turn-off CEMP-s star with [Mg/Fe] = 1.85 dex. For the star SDSS J012630.30+073029.3 ([Fe/H]= -3.02 dex), we have a clear detection of lithium with A(Li) = 2.05. Kinematically, SDSS J214340.08-002835.5 is a thick-disc star, while the other two belong to the halo and are candidate members of the Gaia- Sausage-Enceladus.

AI.tldr: Abundance analysis of three extremely metal-poor turn-off stars using Subaru/HDS spectra confirms them as genuine EMP stars; one is a CEMP-s star with a record-high [Mg/Fe], one shows clear Li detection, and their kinematics link them to the thick disc or the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus halo.
AI.motivation: To determine the detailed chemical composition and kinematics of a sample of extremely metal-poor (EMP) candidate stars selected from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), thereby confirming their nature and constraining their Galactic origin.
AI.method: High-resolution spectroscopy of three faint turn-off stars was obtained with the High-Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) on the Subaru telescope. Standard 1D model atmospheres were used to derive abundances of Li, C, Mg, Ca, Sr, and Ba. Radial velocities were measured and combined with Gaia astrometric data to compute actions and Galactic orbits.
AI.result: The stars have metallicities [Fe/H] between -3.02 and -3.57 dex, confirming them as genuine EMP stars. SDSS J074238.68+470537.0 is classified as a CEMP-s star with [Mg/Fe] = 1.85 dex, the highest ever measured in a turn-off CEMP-s star. SDSS J012630.30+073029.3 ([Fe/H] = -3.02 dex) shows a clear Li detection with A(Li) = 2.05. Kinematically, SDSS J214340.08-002835.5 is a thick-disc star, while the other two belong to the halo and are candidate members of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus.
AI.conclusion: The three SDSS-selected candidates are confirmed as genuine EMP stars with distinct chemical peculiarities (CEMP-s enrichment, Li detection) and diverse kinematic origins, including the thick disc and the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus halo.

title: Common Envelope Evolution: Too stochastic to be deterministic
comment: It will be submitted in two days to allow for comments (including missing references)
summary: I argue for significant stochastic behavior in the common envelope evolution (CEE) of cool giants and main-sequence companions to the degree that it is almost impossible to know the exact CEE outcome of an individual binary system from the average properties of the stars and their initial orbit. I start with two observational properties of post-CEE planetary nebulae: many have jet-shaped morphologies, and they show a wide variety of morphologies. The first suggests that the standard CEE model should include jets, and the second shows that the CEE has a wide variety of evolutionary routes; for example, jets can be launched before, during, and/or after the main CEE phase. I show that the properties of the disk with which the main-sequence companion enters the CEE depend sensitively and stochastically on the pulsations and convection of the giant star. Pulsations and giant-envelope convection stochastically determine the evolution of the accretion disk inside the envelope. The stochastic nature of the accretion disk properties implies that jet power is also stochastic. Adopting the view that jets play a major role in CEE outcomes, I conclude that the CEE outcome is stochastic. I conclude that the CEE efficiency parameter alpha(CE) has little merit for individual systems, although it still has meaning in population synthesis and other studies of large populations.

AI.tldr: The common envelope evolution (CEE) outcome of individual binary systems is argued to be fundamentally stochastic, driven by the chaotic influence of giant-star pulsations and convection on the accretion disk and resulting jets, rendering the efficiency parameter alpha(CE) meaningless for single systems but still useful for population studies.
AI.motivation: Two observational properties of post-CEE planetary nebulae motivate this work: many exhibit jet-shaped morphologies, implying the standard CEE model should incorporate jets, and they display a wide variety of morphologies, indicating that CEE follows diverse evolutionary pathways (e.g., jets launched before, during, and/or after the main CEE phase). This suggests a need to reconsider whether CEE outcomes can be predicted deterministically.
AI.method: The author analyzes how the properties of the accretion disk with which the main-sequence companion enters the CEE depend on the pulsations and convection of the giant star. The stochastic nature of these stellar processes is traced through their effect on the evolution of the accretion disk inside the envelope, and consequently on jet power, adopting the view that jets play a major role in CEE outcomes.
AI.result: Pulsations and giant-envelope convection stochastically determine the evolution of the accretion disk inside the envelope. Because disk properties are stochastic, jet power is also stochastic, and since jets play a major role in CEE outcomes, the CEE outcome itself is stochastic. This makes it nearly impossible to determine the exact CEE outcome of an individual binary from the average properties of the stars and their initial orbit.
AI.conclusion: The CEE efficiency parameter alpha(CE) has little merit for individual systems, since the outcome cannot be reliably predicted from average stellar and orbital properties. However, alpha(CE) retains meaning in population synthesis and other studies of large populations, where stochasticity averages out.

title: Near-infrared periodicity in the SPICY catalog. True young stellar objects versus contaminants
summary: Infrared (IR) large-sky surveys allow study of how localized star formation is, enabling searches for young stellar objects (YSOs) not only at the centers of known stellar nurseries but also across the Galactic plane. However, these spatially unbiased searches suffer from contamination, most notably from dusty asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars characterized by long-period variability. Using time-series analysis, and taking advantage of the different variability timescales of YSOs against long-period variables (LPVs), we assess the level of contamination of one of the most spatially unbiased YSO catalogs (\textit{Spitzer}/IRAC Candidate YSO, SPICY). Distinguishing between these two groups lets us draw more robust conclusions about the frequency of isolated YSOs in our Galaxy and their implications. We cross-match the SPICY and VIRAC2 catalogs (VVV/VVVX Survey), build near-IR light curves for common sources, and compute their periods and amplitudes. Contaminants are identified as sources with periodic flux variations with periods $P\geq 80\,d$ and amplitudes $ΔK_{\rm s}\geq0.35\,\rm{mag}$. From $58\,737$ common sources, we identify $742$ SPICY objects as LPV contaminants based on their long-period variability, and identify $307$ high-confidence periodic YSO candidates exhibiting short-period flux changes consistent with cool spots. Near- and mid-IR amplitudes are correlated only among LPVs, suggesting a common pulsation origin. In addition, the spatial distribution of the identified populations further supports our classification, with LPVs preferentially associated with the bulge and YSOs at the lowest galactic latitudes.

AI.tldr: Time-series analysis of SPICY and VIRAC2 cross-matched sources separates 742 long-period-variable AGB contaminants from 307 high-confidence periodic YSO candidates, enabling more robust conclusions about isolated star formation in the Galaxy.
AI.motivation: IR large-sky surveys enable spatially unbiased searches for YSOs across the Galactic plane, but such searches are contaminated, most notably by dusty AGB stars with long-period variability. Quantifying and removing this contamination is necessary to draw robust conclusions about the frequency of isolated YSOs and their implications.
AI.method: The authors cross-match the SPICY (Spitzer/IRAC Candidate YSO) and VIRAC2 (VVV/VVVX) catalogs, build near-IR light curves for common sources, and compute periods and amplitudes. Contaminants are classified as periodic sources with P ≥ 80 d and ΔK_s ≥ 0.35 mag, exploiting the differing variability timescales of YSOs versus long-period variables.

Near- and mid-IR amplitudes are correlated only among LPVs, indicating a common pulsation origin. The spatial distribution supports the classification: LPVs preferentially associate with the bulge, whereas YSOs concentrate at the lowest Galactic latitudes.
AI.conclusion: Variability-based time-series classification effectively separates AGB/LPV contaminants from genuine YSOs in spatially unbiased IR YSO catalogs, yielding a cleaner sample that strengthens inferences about the frequency and distribution of isolated star formation in the Galaxy.

title: Solar spicule population properties inferred from IRIS Mg II k off-limb spectra using likelihood-free Bayesian inference
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Solar spicules are ubiquitous and strongly overlapping in off-limb observations, which complicates the interpretation of individual events. We aim to infer population-level properties of spicules from IRIS Mg~II~k off-limb spectra using a forward model that explicitly accounts for line-of-sight superposition and instrumental effects. We construct a stochastic three-dimensional spicule-population model and synthesize Mg II k spectra with radiative transfer, including instrumental degradation and photon noise. We then constrain the hyperparameters that describe the underlying spicule population with likelihood-free Bayesian inference based on approximate Bayesian computation and an adaptive population Monte Carlo sampler, comparing observed and simulated datasets through principal-component summary statistics at five heights above the limb. The inferred posterior constrains effective population-level properties of the spicules that dominate the observed Mg II k variability and height dependence. These constraints provide a route to connect off-limb spectroscopy with forthcoming spectropolarimetric diagnostics of the chromosphere-corona interface.

AI.tldr: A stochastic 3D spicule-population forward model, combined with likelihood-free Bayesian inference on IRIS Mg II k off-limb spectra, constrains population-level spicule properties while accounting for line-of-sight superposition and instrumental effects.
AI.motivation: Spicules are ubiquitous and strongly overlapping in off-limb observations, which complicates interpretation of individual events; the paper aims to infer population-level properties instead.
AI.method: Constructs a stochastic 3D spicule-population model and synthesizes Mg II k spectra via radiative transfer, including instrumental degradation and photon noise; constrains hyperparameters using likelihood-free Bayesian inference with approximate Bayesian computation and an adaptive population Monte Carlo sampler, comparing observed and simulated datasets via principal-component summary statistics at five heights above the limb.
AI.result: The inferred posterior constrains effective population-level properties of the spicules that dominate the observed Mg II k variability and height dependence.
AI.conclusion: These constraints provide a route to connect off-limb spectroscopy with forthcoming spectropolarimetric diagnostics of the chromosphere-corona interface.

title: Detection of fine-structured radio bursts during a superflare on EQ Peg
summary: Superflares are frequently observed on magnetically active stars, particularly on active M-dwarfs, thereby influencing the habitability of nearby exoplanets. However, the causes of superflares remain unclear. Here, combining FAST and TESS, we detected a finely structured decimetric radio burst appearing as groups of spikes during a white-light superflare (total bolometric energy $\sim 10^{33} \ \mathrm{erg}$) on the M-dwarf binary EQ Peg on September 8th, 2022. The most significant ones appeared near the peak time of the optical flare and lasted for about $100 \ \mathrm{s}$. The radio spikes present extremely high brightness temperatures ($\gtrsim 10^{13} \ \mathrm{K}$) and high degrees of circular polarization ($\sim 0.84 \pm 0.16$), indicating the origin of a coherent emission process, most likely the electron cyclotron maser. Based on Zeeman-Doppler Imaging measurements of EQ Peg, we further locate the sources of the radio spikes, including their heights and latitudes, under the assumption of a large-scale dipolar magnetic field configuration. The results provide strong evidence for finely structured decimetric radio bursts generated by stellar flares and shed light on the origin of superflares.

AI.tldr: Combining FAST and TESS observations, the authors detected finely structured decimetric radio spikes during a white-light superflare on the M-dwarf binary EQ Peg, with brightness temperatures ≳10^13 K and high circular polarization, indicating coherent emission (likely electron cyclotron maser). Using Zeeman-Doppler Imaging, they located the radio sources' heights and latitudes under a dipolar field assumption, providing evidence linking such radio bursts to stellar flares and superflare origins.
AI.motivation: Superflares are frequently observed on magnetically active stars, especially active M-dwarfs, and affect the habitability of nearby exoplanets. Despite their importance, the physical causes of superflares remain unclear. Studying the radio signatures associated with superflares can help reveal the underlying emission mechanisms and origins.
AI.method: The study combined FAST (radio) and TESS (optical) observations to detect a decimetric radio burst during a white-light superflare on the M-dwarf binary EQ Peg on September 8th, 2022. The radio burst appeared as groups of spikes near the optical flare peak, lasting about 100 s. The authors analyzed brightness temperatures and circular polarization to infer the emission process, and used Zeeman-Doppler Imaging measurements of EQ Peg to locate the radio spike sources (heights and latitudes) assuming a large-scale dipolar magnetic field configuration.
AI.result: A finely structured decimetric radio burst composed of spike groups was detected during a white-light superflare with total bolometric energy ~10^33 erg. The most significant spikes occurred near the optical flare peak and lasted ~100 s. The radio spikes showed extremely high brightness temperatures (≳10^13 K) and high circular polarization (~0.84 ± 0.16), indicating coherent emission, most likely electron cyclotron maser. The sources of the radio spikes were further located in height and latitude based on Zeeman-Doppler Imaging under a dipolar field assumption.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide strong evidence for finely structured decimetric radio bursts generated by stellar flares and shed light on the origin of superflares on magnetically active stars such as M-dwarfs.
